messages:
Jules (sales): Polaris POC blocked: intermittent TLS handshake failures + some requests hit 429s from our side during load tests. They repro from private endpoint only. Need a quick triage before EOW demo.

Polaris-Security: We see two symptoms: (1) from app subnet X: TLS alert 'unknown CA' intermittently; (2) from app subnet Y: 429 Too Many Requests from your API. Both to private.redwood-polaris.internal. Here's curl from failing host X:

Polaris-Security: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-polaris.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private.redwood-polaris.internal/health
* Connected to 10.6.7.11 (10.6.7.11) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLS 1.3 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA (542)
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'corp-proxy.local' does not match target host name 'private.redwood-polaris.internal'```

Iris (neteng): That suggests TLS interception on some egress paths. Which subnets route via corporate transit?

Polaris-Security: Subnet X -> transit + inspection (fails). Subnet Y -> direct NAT -> reaches private endpoint but sometimes gets 429 during a 100rps test. We captured headers for the 429s: X-RateLimit-Limit: 100, X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0, X-RateLimit-Reset: 1619999999.

Noah (eng-platform): 429s mean our rate limiter is counting requests by client IP or token. Private endpoints from transit may SNAT to a shared egress IP and hit a shared limit. Are they using many pods behind a single NAT?

Polaris-Security: Yes, many pods share a NAT gateway. But the 429s appeared even when the test was below the per-account quota. Logs show per-source-ip buckets bursting.

Rohit (solutions): Two parallel threads: TLS MITM for Subnet X and rate-limiter contention for Subnet Y. For TLS MITM short-term: either have them bypass inspection for our POC IP /32 or have them trust the inspection CA on test hosts. For rate limits: we can provision a dedicated POC IP so their NAT doesn't collide with other tenants; or we can temporarily raise rate limit for this trial. Which is preferable?

Polaris-Security: Bypass is possible but needs change control. Raising rate limits temporarily is allowed if you supply an IP allowlist and we know the exact window. Trusting CA across dozens of hosts is not feasible for tomorrow.

Iris (neteng): We prefer a single /32 bypass plus a spike allowance on your side. If you provide the POC IP we can add it to the corp egress bypass and exempt it from MITM. Also we can whitelist that IP in our WAF to prevent shared-NAT 429s hitting you.

Noah (eng-platform): We can spin an ALB with IP 203.0.115.21 and ensure it terminates TLS with a cert matching private.redwood-polaris.internal. We'll also route rate limiting by client IP not by shared egress IP for that endpoint. deploy-bot: queued create-poc-alb(203.0.115.21) -> status: queued.

Rohit (solutions): If you change rate-limiter logic to prefer token over source IP and we also add the dedicated IP, that should cover both symptoms. Can we toggle rate-limiting policy for the POC route quickly?

Noah (eng-platform): Yes, we have a per-route override. For the POC route we'll use token-based buckets (API key id) and increase limits to 500 rps for 2 hours. I'll annotate in the config.

Polaris-Security: Provide SLA: we want the exact IP, window, and cert SANs. Also send a security note explaining why bypass is only temporary and that you will revoke the cert and remove the IP afterwards.

Noah (eng-platform): IP: 203.0.115.21. Window: 48 hours starting 2026-03-27T14:00Z. Cert SANs: private.redwood-polaris.internal and poc-polaris.safe. We'll revoke after window. deploy-bot: allocation approved -> provisioning ALB (203.0.115.21).

Iris (neteng): Change control: applying bypass for 203.0.115.21/32 to skip MITM and remove WAF rate-limit on that IP. ETA 30m. Who to ping when complete?

Jules (sales): Ping this thread and DM me the IC for sign-off. I'll confirm with Polaris contacts.

Polaris-Security: Bypass in place. Test output from previously failing host X now:

Polaris-Security: ```curl -v https://private.redwood-polaris.internal/health
* Connected to 203.0.115.21 (203.0.115.21) port 443
* TLS handshake complete
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
{ "status": "ok" }```

Polaris-Security: Load test from Subnet Y (500rps) against the dedicated IP: no 429s, responses at expected p95 latency. Headers show X-RateLimit-Remaining > 100.

Rohit (solutions): Great. Next steps: 1) Noah revert rate-limiter policy after the demo window and log changes; 2) Noah revoke cert + tear down ALB at window end; 3) Iris / Polaris document long-term approach (private hosted zone assoc or resolver) and whether they want a persistent dedicated IP for production.

Noah (eng-platform): Noted. I'll add the rollout/rollback entries and the revocation job. deploy-bot: schedule tear-down(203.0.115.21) -> 2026-03-29T14:05Z.

ops-bot: reminder: temporary IP 203.0.115.21 scheduled for teardown 2026-03-29T14:05Z.

Jules (sales): Thanks team 1: demo is green. I'll capture this in the deal ticket and send the security notes. :tada:
